<Route path="/ade/dashboard/projects" />

A **project** is one API: its classes, paths and every version of it. **Go to Build → Projects** to
see them all. The header sums them up — for example *2 projects · avg quality 83 · 2 active*.

<Screenshot id="projects" alt="The Projects page in Cards view: two project cards with quality, lint and debt scores, a New project card and the portfolio quality trend" />

## Find a project

- **Search** with the filter box (<Kbd keys="/"/> focuses it).
- **Filter** with **All**, **Active**, **Needs attention** and **Deleted**. **Deleted** works once
  **Show deleted** is on.
- **Sort** with **Sorted by name ↑**.
- **Switch views** with **Cards** (the default) and **Table**.

<Screenshot id="projects-table" alt="The Projects page in Table view: columns for project, description, quality trend, versions, owner, status and creator, with the Owner filter in the toolbar" />

The table shows **Project**, **Description**, **Quality trend**, **Versions**, **Status**, **Created
by** and **Updated**. **Portfolio quality trend** under the list plots average quality across
projects after each import.

**Click a project** to open its [versions](./versions.mdx).

## Create a project

1. **Click “New project”** (or press <Kbd keys="N"/>).
2. On **Create manually**, choose a **Starting template** — **Blank** starts empty.
3. Enter a **Project name** (for example `Payments API`); the **Slug** (`payments-api`) is suggested
   from it. **Description** and **Domain category** are optional.
4. Fill in **API metadata (OpenAPI info)** if you know it — **API summary**, contact and licence.
   It becomes the spec's `info` block, and you can change it later.
5. **Click “Create project”.**

<Screenshot id="projects-create-dialog" alt="The New project dialog: starting template, project name, slug, description and API metadata fields" />

**Design with AI** (marked *Beta*) drafts a project from a description instead. To start from a
file you already have, **click “Import”** — see [Import your first
project](../getting-started/first-project.mdx).

## Edit, delete and restore

Open a project's menu (**⋯** on a card or row):

| Item | Does |
| --- | --- |
| **Open versions** | Opens the project's [Versions](./versions.mdx) (table view) |
| **Consumers** | Who depends on this API — see below |
| **Edit project** | Changes the name, description and API metadata; **“Save changes”** |
| **Delete project** | Moves it to **Deleted**. Turn on **Show deleted** to find it again |
| **Undelete project** | Brings a deleted project back |
| **Permanently delete** | Removes it for good — type the slug, then **“Delete everything”** |

In the table, tick rows to **Delete** or **Undelete** several at once.

## Consumers

<Route path="/ade/dashboard/projects/[projectId]/consumers" />

**Consumers** lists the teams and services that depend on the API, and which operations and fields
each one uses. **“Register consumer”** adds one by hand; **“Import Pact file”** adds one from a
consumer contract.

## Owner

A project can have an owner team. CODEOWNERS rules for the spec's path and the document's own
`x-apiome-owner` extension *suggest* one, and a suggestion becomes the owner only when someone
confirms it.

**In a list**, the **Owner** column (on cards, a line under the summary) names the team. A
*suggested* owner carries a **Suggested** badge saying where it came from — *Gateway tag*,
*CODEOWNERS*, *Spec* — and a **“Confirm”** button: **click “Confirm”** to make it the owner; the
row updates in place. The team's name opens its [team page](../workspace/teams.mdx#team-pages).

**Owner** in the toolbar shows one team's projects (kept in the address as `?team=`). In **Table**
view, tick projects and use **Assign owner** in the bar at the bottom of the page to give them all
the same owner.

On a project's **Consumers**, the **Owner** column is the consumer's owner team and **Contact** is
the free-text owner it was registered with; **Owner** in the toolbar filters by team there too. See
[Teams → Ownership](../workspace/teams.mdx#ownership).

## With the CLI or the API

- CLI: `apiome projects list`, `apiome projects get <id>`, `apiome projects update
  <slug-or-id>` to change a project's name, slug (`--rename`), description or domain, and
  `apiome projects delete <slug-or-id>` to delete one, and `apiome projects export <slug-or-id>` to
  back the whole project up as one document ([format](../reference/cli-export-format.md)) — see the
  [`projects` command reference](../reference/cli/projects.md) and the [CLI
  quick-start](../reference/cli-quickstart.md).
- REST: `GET` / `POST /v1/projects/{tenant}`, `GET` / `PUT` / `DELETE
  /v1/projects/{tenant}/{project}`, `POST /v1/projects/{tenant}/{project}/restore` — see the [API
  reference](../reference/api-reference.md). `DELETE` is a soft delete (undone with `restore`);
  `DELETE …?permanent=true` removes the project and everything under it for good, and
  `GET …/{project}/deletion-impact` counts what that would remove. A `PUT` may carry `expectedUpdatedAt` (the
  project's `updated_at` as you last read it); if the project has changed since, nothing is
  written and the response is `409` with code `update_conflict`.

### Update a project from the CLI

1. **Preview** the change: `apiome projects update payments-api --description 'Charges,
   refunds, payouts.' --domain finance --dry-run` prints each changed field as a `-` / `+` pair
   and sends nothing.
2. **Apply** it by running the same command without `--dry-run`.
3. To **change the slug**, add `--rename payments-v2`. The CLI asks you to confirm (pass
   `--yes` in scripts): links, scripts and commands that use the old slug stop working, because
   there is no redirect.
4. To edit several fields at once, **dump** the project with `apiome --json projects get <id> >
   project.json`, edit `name`, `slug`, `description`, `enabled` or `metadata`, and **apply** it
   with `apiome projects update <id> --from-file project.json`. If someone changed the project
   after your dump, nothing is written and the command exits `6` — dump it again and re-apply.

### Delete a project from the CLI

`apiome projects delete <slug-or-id>` first shows what will be removed — the project's versions
(and how many are published), classes, properties and paths.

1. **Archive** — a soft delete you can undo on the Projects page (turn on **Show deleted**, then **Undelete project**):
   `apiome projects delete payments-api --archive`, then answer **y**.
2. **Delete permanently** — `apiome projects delete payments-api`, then **type the project slug**
   (`payments-api`, exactly — it is case-sensitive). In a script, pass `--yes` instead; the
   argument must then be the exact slug, not the project's id.
3. A project with **published versions** is refused — the command exits `6` — because consumers can
   still fetch those specs. Unpublish them first, or add `--force`. This applies to `--archive` too.
4. A permanent delete is refused if the project's versions have **audit history**, which Apiome
   never deletes; archive the project instead.

With `--json`, a successful delete prints `{"deleted": true, "slug": "payments-api",
"permanent": true}`.
